documents.title: Tired, achy joints, rash
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'd like to come in. I've been really tired for months now - since around the fall - and my joints ache, mostly my wrists and knees. I also keep getting a red rash across my cheeks after I've been outside in the sun, like after recess duty. It fades after a day or two. My aunt has lupus so I'm a little worried.

documents.title: RE: Tired, achy joints, rash
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Nilda, thanks for letting us know. I've booked you with your doctor on 3/21 at 1:20 pm. If you develop fever, chest pain or shortness of breath before then, please call us right away.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
OFFICE VISIT

CC: fatigue, joint pain, facial rash.

HPI: 35F with APL in remission (2018) presents with roughly 5 months of tiredness that sleep doesn't fix and aching joints - wrists and knees mostly. Separately notices a red rash across her cheeks after time outdoors in the sun, lasting a day or two. No fevers. No bleeding or bruising. Maternal aunt has SLE.

Meds: folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 units.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 121/67, HR 63, T 36.4, wt 62.0 kg.
Skin: no rash on the face today. Wrists and knees: no swelling or effusion, full range of motion. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender. No lymphadenopathy.

A/P:
Fatigue + inflammatory-sounding arthralgia + photosensitive facial rash by history, FH of SLE -> concerned for lupus.
- Rheumatology referral placed; asked front desk to push for an early slot. Rheumatology does its own serologies and baseline labs at the consult, so not drawing today.
- Sun protection: broad-spectrum sunscreen, hat for recess duty.
- Call if fever, chest pain, worsening joints.

documents.title: Referral scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Rheumatology accepted referral. Consult 4/11 at 10:30. Called pt, she has the date and address. Asked to arrive 15 min early for labs paperwork.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (200 mg) by mouth once daily

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/11/2023
Patient: Nilda Mendez, 35-year-old woman
Referred by: primary care, for fatigue, joint pain and facial rash

Thank you for sending Ms. Mendez to us.

History: She describes about six months of tiredness along with aching in her joints, worst in the wrists and knees, and a rash over her face that comes and goes after she has been out in the sun. She has a history of acute promyelocytic leukemia diagnosed in 2018, treated and in remission.

Medications: folic acid 1 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother with rheumatoid arthritis; maternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus; father with hypertension.
Social: elementary school teacher. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: BP 109/78, pulse 70, weight 61.5 kg. Malar rash over both cheeks and the nasal bridge. Mild synovitis of both wrists and both knees. No oral ulcers. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

Laboratory (drawn here 04/11/2023):
- Hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL (low)
- White blood cells 3,500/uL (low)
- Platelets 100,000/uL (low)
- ANA positive, titer 1:640
- Anti-dsDNA positive
- C3 low, C4 low
- Creatinine 0.78 mg/dL
- Urinalysis negative for protein and blood

Impression: Systemic lupus erythematosus, with malar rash and photosensitivity, inflammatory arthritis of the wrists and knees, and leukopenia, anemia and thrombocytopenia that I attribute to lupus. Strongly positive ANA, positive dsDNA and low complements support the diagnosis. Kidney function and urine are normal.

Plan:
1. Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, started today.
2. Strict sun protection - broad-spectrum sunscreen, hat, avoid midday sun.
3. Baseline retinal examination for hydroxychloroquine - referral to ophthalmology placed.
4. Return in about 3 months with CBC, C3/C4, creatinine and urinalysis.

Medications at the end of this visit: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily (new today); folic acid 1 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.

Rheumatology

documents.title: New lupus medicine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, rheumatology told me I have lupus and started me on hydroxychloroquine. I'm still trying to get pregnant. Is this medicine safe if I do get pregnant? I forgot to ask there. Kind of overwhelmed.

documents.title: RE: New lupus medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Nilda, I got the rheumatology letter - I'm sorry, that's a lot to take in at once. Hydroxychloroquine is one of the lupus medicines that is generally continued in pregnancy, so it's not a reason to stop trying. Do keep taking it every day, and please also ask rheumatology at your next visit so they can plan with you. Happy to talk by phone or in person if helpful.

documents.title: Ophthalmology - baseline exam
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY
Date of exam: 05/22/2023
Reason: baseline examination before long-term hydroxychloroquine (SLE).

Visual acuity: 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. IOP normal OU. Anterior segment unremarkable OU.
Dilated fundus exam: optic nerves healthy; maculae normal with no pigmentary change; periphery flat.
SD-OCT macula: normal foveal contour and outer retinal layers OU.
Automated visual fields 10-2: full OU.

Impression: normal baseline examination; no evidence of retinopathy.
Plan: annual hydroxychloroquine screening beginning after 5 years of use, sooner if visual symptoms.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 07/13/2023

Ms. Mendez returns 3 months after starting hydroxychloroquine for SLE. Joint pain much improved, energy coming back, and she has had no new facial rash using sun protection. Taking hydroxychloroquine daily without side effects.

Exam: BP 108/67, weight 61.9 kg. No rash. No synovitis. Heart and lungs normal.

Labs 07/13/2023: WBC 4.9, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 218 - counts back to normal. C3 and C4 normal. Creatinine 0.76. Urinalysis without protein or blood.
Ophthalmology baseline exam normal.

Assessment: SLE responding well to hydroxychloroquine. Cytopenias, including the thrombocytopenia, have resolved.
Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily. Labs and visit in about 3 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL - 35F

Interval: diagnosed with SLE by rheumatology 4/2023 - started hydroxychloroquine; joints and fatigue much better, counts normalized per rheum 7/2023. Baseline eye exam normal. Still trying to conceive, about a year now; on folic acid.
No bruising/bleeding. No rash this summer with sun protection.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily (rheum), folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BP 104/77, HR 67, wt 62.2 kg.
Well. No malar rash. Joints without swelling. CV RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no organomegaly. Skin no petechiae. Neuro grossly intact.

PHQ-9: 3.

A/P:
1. SLE - stable on HCQ, rheum following q3 mo.
2. APL in CR - CBC today.
3. Preventive: CMP. Flu and updated COVID vaccine in the fall. Cervical screening due 2024.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Nilda - blood counts are back where they belong (hemoglobin 13.4, white count 5.0, platelets 221); the MCH flagged a touch high at 31.3, a red cell measure that isn't a concern. Kidney and liver tests are normal. Glad the hydroxychloroquine is working.

documents.title: Flu and COVID vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine IM L deltoid; updated COVID-19 vaccine IM R deltoid. Pt on hydroxychloroquine - no contraindication. Not pregnant per pt. VIS given, tolerated well, observed 15 min.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 10/24/2023

SLE on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily. Doing well - no joint swelling, no rash, energy normal. Adherent.

Exam: BP 117/70, weight 62.5 kg. No synovitis, skin clear.
Labs: CBC normal (WBC 4.8, Hgb 12.7, plt 186). C3, C4 normal. Creatinine 0.8. UA negative for protein and blood.

Assessment/plan: quiescent SLE. Continue hydroxychloroquine. Return in 3-4 months with labs.

orders.reason: Not pregnant after about 17 months of trying

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
OFFICE VISIT

CC: not pregnant yet.

35F, SLE (quiet on HCQ), APL in CR. Trying to conceive since about 7/2022 - roughly 17 months - without a pregnancy. Periods are regular, every 28 days, normal flow. No pelvic pain. On folic acid 1 mg daily.

Exam: BP 106/69, HR 63, wt 61.8 kg. Well-appearing. Thyroid not enlarged. No galactorrhea reported.

A/P: more than a year of trying without pregnancy at 35 -> referral to gynecology for evaluation. She'd prefer to go straight to them for the workup labs. Referral placed; continue folic acid.

conditions.label: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
conditions.note: Diminished ovarian reserve: low AMH, low-normal estradiol, FSH 14.8; regular 28-day cycles

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/10/2024
Reason for referral: no pregnancy after about 18 months of trying.

Many thanks for referring Ms. Mendez. She is a 35-year-old woman who has been trying for a year and a half without conceiving, even though her periods come like clockwork every 28 days. Her history includes systemic lupus erythematosus, quiet on hydroxychloroquine, and acute promyelocytic leukemia treated in 2018 and in remission. Medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily. No known drug allergies.
Family history: her mother went through menopause at 38.

Examination: BP 103/78, weight 62.5 kg. General, breast, abdominal and pelvic examinations are unremarkable.

Laboratory (cycle day 3, drawn 01/10/2024):
- TSH 1.7 - normal
- Prolactin 11.9 - normal
- Estradiol - low-normal
- Anti-Mullerian hormone - low
- FSH 14.8 mIU/mL - elevated for early follicular phase

Assessment: diminished ovarian reserve, with an elevated early-follicular FSH, low AMH and low-normal estradiol - hypergonadotropic hypogonadism - in a woman with regular ovulatory-pattern cycles.

Plan: I went through these results with her and what they mean, and we discussed her options in general terms. She would like time to think things over. No treatment started today and no further referral at this time.

Gynecology

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 02/15/2024

SLE, stable. No arthritis, rash, mouth sores or chest symptoms since last visit. Taking hydroxychloroquine daily.

Exam: BP 114/70, wt 61.8 kg. Unremarkable; no synovitis.
Labs: CBC - WBC 5.4, Hgb 13.3, plt 204; MCH 31.1, marginally above range, not significant. C3 and C4 normal. Creatinine 0.84. UA: no protein, no blood.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily. Follow up 4 months.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt no-showed 3/12 4:20 pm follow-up. Called - she apologized, forgot because of parent-teacher conferences that afternoon. Says rheumatology is seeing her every few months and she's feeling fine; would rather just come for her annual physical in the summer. Booked annual 8/15 9:40. Routed to PCP FYI.

Date of service: 06/05/2024

Lupus remains quiet on hydroxychloroquine. School year wrapping up; feels well.
Exam: BP 108/66, pulse 74. Joints normal, no rash.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL - 36F

Interval: SLE quiet on HCQ per rheumatology (seen 6/2024, labs normal). Seen by gyn 1/2024 - diminished ovarian reserve, labeled hypergonadotropic hypogonadism; cycles remain regular, no treatment. No hospitalizations.
Feels well. No bruising, bleeding, joint swelling or rash.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BP 116/75, HR 66, wt 62.1 kg.
Gen well. HEENT normal. Neck no LAD. CV RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts deferred per pt preference, no concerns. Abd soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing; cytology/HPV co-test collected. Skin clear. Ext no edema.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. Cervical cancer screening - co-test sent (last 2019 normal).
2. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipid panel.
3. SLE, APL in CR, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism - stable; specialists following as above.
4. Vaccines: flu + updated COVID this fall.
Folic acid refilled. RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Nilda - your cervical screening came back normal (no abnormal cells, HPV not detected), so the next one isn't due for 5 years. Blood counts are healthy (the monocyte percentage is a hair over the lab's range at 9%, which means nothing by itself), kidney and liver tests are normal, and cholesterol is fine (LDL 97).

documents.title: Flu and COVID vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza (trivalent) IM left deltoid and 2024-25 COVID-19 vaccine IM right deltoid. No contraindications on screening. VIS provided. No reaction during 15 min observation.
